newsitem.title: USA: BankBoston ups Ecuador debt to overweight.
newsitem.headline: BankBoston ups Ecuador debt to overweight.

text.p: BankBoston Corp said it upgraded its position on Ecuador's Brady debt to overweight from neutral.

"The favorable contrast between the populist electoral rhetoric of President Abdal Bucaram and the initiatives he has taken since his inauguration on August 10 prompt us to revise our opinion on Ecuador's credit quality," said Peter Allen, head of BankBoston's emerging markets research.
BankBoston said it had maintained a cautious approach following Bucaram's inauguration on August 10 because it had been concerned about a lack of continuity in economic policy.

BankBoston had lowered its rating to neutral following Bucaram's appointment of Pablo Concha as Finance Minister, but the firm said Concha has established a good working relationship with Central Bank President Augusto de la Torre.

"In 1997, we anticipate significant improvement in the quality of economic policy and also expect the implementation of a convertibility scheme similar to Argentina's," added Allen, who is also a managing director at the company.

BankBoston said it believes that this turn of events should improve credit quality over the next six months and give rise to at least 100 basis points of spread tightening on Ecuador's Brady debt in the next three months.
Ecuador has performed well in recent months, but the firm said the country's Bradies still have the widest spreads in Latin America and have further potential to narrow.
